venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Tuesday 8/18 (MOD: MKZ, entered by Mya)** A very hot and chill Tuesday at Close Company Atlanta. Quiet opening shift. Got a nice crowd for Bingo but nothing crazy — mostly the same regulars, which we love to see. Opener left around 7pm with closer and MOD holding it down; barback handled prep. Smooth close overall. Reminders: throw broken glasses in the designated area, and make sure tabs are sent to the kitchen rather than sitting on the screen. Kitchen: quiet day; communicate with FOH when ticket times get long. Maintenance: BOH sink leaking. 86'd/low: none. No incidents or injuries. Favorite moment: meeting some locals, Carlos and Josh.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Tuesday 8/18 (MOD/Chef: KK / JMS, entered by BC)** Decent Tuesday service. We missed our expected wave closer to end of service. We hosted several bingo regulars, one of whom brought colleagues from out of town, plus a lot of new faces. Emily from the Nashventures IG joined during this time with Hayley's replacement and played bingo. After bingo we closed most guests out; our bingo host stayed with a group of friends celebrating her birthday. Room began clearing again ~10:30pm and the last guest left at 11:10pm. Several industry guests throughout the night. Comps $131.70 / 10.3% (marketing, bingo credit, industry). Kitchen: John Michael held it down even with stitches — phenomenal. 86: Miller High Life, cider, Tanqueray. Low: Vida, Tripping Gold. No incidents. Favorite moment: our bingo host celebrating her birthday with us.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Tuesday 8/18 (AM: Maggie S, Evan, Josh, Lucas; PM: Maggie H & Chef Rachel)** AM/Marquee $1,162.00, D&C PM $7,140.90, total net sales $8,302.90 plus $1,650 net event sales = $9,952.90 against a $7,863 target. Food $2,233.20 plus $1,455 event food = $3,688.20. AM notes: Tuesday was a breeze — good pops in the first half, mellow finish. Made peach cardi and fresh cold brew, new lemon juice bottle; coffee, tea, to-go goods, Saratoga and chai ordered. Low: Saratoga, matcha. 86: evergreen, kombucha. D&C notes: 9p never came for us, busiest hours were 6-7pm, but the team still cleared the sales goal by a few hundred before event revenue. Techs out tomorrow to fix the pebble ice machine; the group that arrived a day early for their Garden event may return tomorrow. Kitchen: epic day, deep cleaning done on downtime, chill prep day. Low: cola dip, chicken breast, burger portions, onion jam fix, cherry redux. 911: scallop, rabbit, creamed spinach, burger meat. 86: rabbit. Events: Day 2 of 3 of Anaconda LLC meetings tomorrow, 15 guests 8am-5pm in Vauxhall; coffee/hot water/creamers ready at 8am, group staying at the Ramble. No incidents. Favorite moment: Mel visiting Marquee with a friend; Dodgers fans stoked after the game.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Tuesday 8/18 (MOD & Chef: Joe + Vic)** A relatively steady Tuesday night. Started with 30 covers and a decent amount of walk-ins through the first couple of hours. Ariana's first live shift at the host stand and she crushed it — got everyone downstairs fast and made every guest feel at home. Room filled up around 8pm with the bulk of reservations; flow of service was very smooth and we opened the 20s for a bit to accommodate a few groups. Stayed mostly full until about 11pm, then cleared slowly. Comps $111 (Yiban, industry, investor, birthday, DNL). Standing room $0. Kitchen: chill night. No incidents; no-shows charged. Favorite moment: a guest walked in on her boyfriend on a date with someone else, sat down and introduced herself — they all left immediately and he came back down to pay the bill.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.weather: Hot and humid to start, cooled off
venues.narrative: **DC — Tuesday 8/18 (MOD: Marcus)** Marquee bar sales $4,198.55, garden $0, total net sales including events $3,816.87 against a $3,981 target. Food $514. Guests 76 (43 walk-in / 33 reservation). The night started solid with a decent opening pop that carried into a 7pm push — shoutout to the guests who pregamed with us before My Chemical Romance. Around 7:30 we picked up more steam and the room stayed pretty full until about 9, then died off; cut the host at 10 and were down to two tables by 10:30 while breaking down a well. A handful of walk-ins after that, nothing unmanageable. Last call 11:30. Connor did a fantastic job in his closing server training under Devan with support from the whole team. Devon Tarby stuck around for a cheeky bevy and Khaleel stopped by. Kitchen: decent night despite being 86 oysters; James ran food and touched tables. Comps $10 (employee discount). What went well: communication and guest connection. To improve: keep closing and breakdown tasks out of guests' sightlines so the room feels open until the last guest leaves. Maintenance: curtain needs attention again. No incidents.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Tuesday 8/18 (AM: Braden & Shannon; PM: Justin & Shannon)** Municipal Bar morning $679 (22 guests), evening $3,189 (77 guests), Sun Club $142, Hot Eye $0 — total net sales $4,009 against a $4,500 target. Food $1,822. Comps $217.40. Morning: quiet, with a few hotel guests arriving at the same hour for breakfast; Sierra held it down solo and did great. A large food tour at 1pm pushed us into lunch and we cleaned a lot of the mezz glass. Evening: started quiet like yesterday then picked up in the second half. Most reservations were in by 7, walk-ins strong from 8 to 9; about half of guests were hotel. Heads up — a service dog staying in the hotel (black German Shepherd) was a little feisty in the dining room. Madison trained with Tia through the afternoon on finer food details via the info spreadsheets. Sun Club: hot day, slow start, picked up around 1ish, ~6 hotel guests all ordering drinks, no food. Kitchen: some sus oysters went out and got DNL'd, no other notes or 86s. No injuries. Favorite moment: Emma made cute cards for all the reservations celebrating birthdays tonight.
